tech.title: Tech world's calls for Jensen Huang to return to Nvidia are growing
tech.summary: An online petition calling for Jensen Huang's reinstatement as CEO of Nvidia has received more than 160,000 signatures. It has reportedly attracted support from Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan. Huang is currently under investigation into how his actions may have damaged America's AI dominance, the national security implications, and his close relationship with President Trump and his Cabinet. Huang has discussed the possibility of returning, but the investigations surrounding him will likely prevent that from happening.

tech.title: Apple Bets on Siri AI Apps as the Main Draw for Its Smart Glasses
tech.summary: Apple rolled out its new Siri AI earlier as it needs software makers to begin preparing for its smart glasses, which it plans to ship in 2027. The company is counting on integration with apps people already use on their iPhones as a key differentiator for the glasses. Its large developer ecosystem could give it an advantage over Meta and Google's offerings as it potentially provides countless third-party integrations on launch. The hardware for the glasses won't be dramatically different from rival offerings, which makes it more crucial for Apple to nail the developer ecosystem.

tech.title: One Proton Away
tech.summary: Marathon Fusion, a San Francisco-based fusion startup, claims it has created gold from mercury. The startup has not published how much gold it made, and the process requires a fusion plant that does not exist yet. Many fields currently rely on isotopes from aging reactors. Marathon Fusion's process could unlock a world of abundant isotopes, opening up many markets and possibilities.

tech.title: SpaceX Catches Starship in Midair at Texas Site After Space Trip
tech.summary: SpaceX successfully caught Starship using the vehicle's launch tower's mechanical arms on Saturday afternoon. The midair capture serves as a major proof of concept for Starship. SpaceX has now captured both sections of the launch system during different missions. It aborted an attempt to catch Super Heavy during the recent flight due to a slight underperformance of the engines.

tech.title: Outcomes are the new experience
tech.summary: Customers don't care ultimately how quickly their questions are answered. What matters is whether or not they got the outcome they needed. Zendesk's Outcome AI Platform is how industry leading brands are winning the future of customer service. Explore Zendesk Outcome AI

tech.title: Making a programming language
tech.summary: A compiler is a line of small programs. Each turns one shape into the next. The programs transform text into tokens and tokens into a tree, then the tree gets checked, and either an interpreter runs it or it becomes a native binary. No single stage is hard - the work is in making errors useful and keeping two backends in agreement.

tech.title: Building always-on agents
tech.summary: Always-on agents run indefinitely, managing context across sessions and taking action without direct supervision. They have surged in popularity lately, largely due to recent model advancements that have made them more practical to run. Models now have better judgment and are more reliable, and intelligence is becoming cheaper. This post breaks down the primitives behind always-on agents and walks through how they fit together.

tech.title: Become a founding member of TLDR's AI community (2 minute form)
tech.summary: TLDR is launching a curated community for AI builders to discuss major news and launches. The best links and comments will be featured in TLDR AI. Apply here to join .

tech.title: The avalanche that hit math is coming for AI development
tech.summary: AI's capabilities in mathematics exploded quickly. Current AIs can now complete well-scoped problems in mathematics easily. This ability to solve well-scoped problems is going to be an even bigger deal for machine learning research than for mathematics. AI labs mainly care about how any new algorithmic recipe empirically makes training more efficient or elicits smarter models - they don't care about theory for its own sake.

tech.title: AI, work from home, and the young-graduate job market
tech.summary: New college graduates are employed less than a few years ago. While AI may be a factor, there's growing evidence that work from home is an important factor moving the needle on young-graduate employment. AI exposure and teleworkability are highly correlated with each other, making it hard to distinguish definitively between the two factors. The full extent of AI's effects on the labor market might not manifest until the next recession.

tech.summary: New Relic ran the industry's largest observability survey, with over 2,500 respondents. Read to discover the state of "phantom velocity", tool sprawl, and AI ROI. Get the 2026 Observability Forecast

tech.summary: The researchers failed to flag warning signals from a non-human-primate study and didn't disclose the child's death in the published research paper.

tech.title: AI and hiring: bad for employees, bad for employers
tech.summary: AI is flooding processes that require input from the public, causing many to break.

tech.title: Apple Launches New App to Study How People Use AI for Health
tech.summary: The Apple Health AI study will examine comprehension, response quality, the drivers of user trust, and everyday health actions to inform the responsible design of health AI experiences and to explore how health AI might help people prepare for doctor's visits.

tech.title: Recursive, Self, Improvement
tech.summary: This post disentangles the three components involved in recursive self-improvement and shows how the deep learning paradigm forces researchers to consider what counts as the 'self' undergoing improvement.

tech.summary: If recursive self-improvement has started, a broadly beyond-human AGI may arrive in just six to 18 months.

tech.summary: Select customers can now pre-order the golden Cybercab for $29,990, with an estimated delivery in December.

webdev.title: How to Speed Up CI in the Age of AI-Written Code
webdev.summary: AI coding agents produce code faster than CI pipelines can check it, turning long pipelines into queues for developers and agents. Five fixes target the bottleneck: measure slow steps, cache dependencies, use faster runners, parallelize jobs and tests, and skip redundant work with path filters and cancellation. Change one thing at a time and check vendor speed claims against your own pipeline.

webdev.title: Let's Write a PostScript Interpreter
webdev.summary: Build a small PostScript interpreter in JavaScript, starting with tokenization, operand and dictionary stacks, and representations for names, arrays, and procedures. This tutorial adds execution and an interactive REPL, then explores recursion, iteration, and dynamic scope. It deliberately omits graphics, strings, most error handling, and other parts of the full language.

webdev.title: Goal Engineering: How to Design Goals
webdev.summary: Agent feedback becomes a bottleneck when expert knowledge and subjective preferences live only in people's heads. Scope goals around what humans can review efficiently, rather than simply giving each agent more context. In the Actively AI case study, agents organized by job type across accounts let salespeople review similar tasks together and share lessons across their work.

webdev.title: All AI-generated code should be Open Source
webdev.summary: This essay argues that AI-generated code should be released under open-source licenses or dedicated to the public domain because models depend on collectively produced code. It also raises copyright questions while acknowledging that jurisdictions differ and that human involvement varies. The proposal is an argument about how developers should share generated work.

webdev.title: Teach AI coding assistants your design system with Markdown
webdev.summary: Document tokens, component APIs, and composition patterns in Markdown beside the code, then use AGENTS.md to tell coding assistants what to read. A React and Tailwind demo illustrates how automated checks can flag hardcoded colors, unsupported variants, and spacing drift. The examples are constructed rather than a controlled AI experiment, and Markdown guidance still needs maintenance and accessibility review.

webdev.title: Build with TensorWave on AMD
webdev.summary: WaveLabs is where TensorWave's developers building AI on AMD come together. Swap ideas with researchers, get real feedback on your projects, and see how others are making AMD GPUs work. Find practical resources, catch live demos, and connect at events with people tackling the same technical challenges you are.

webdev.summary: TLDR is launching a curated community for AI builders to discuss major news and launches. The best links and comments will be featured in TLDR AI. Apply here to join .

webdev.title: DeepSeek V3 in pure JAX
webdev.summary: A 190-line JAX implementation recreates DeepSeek V3 architecture features, including latent attention, routed experts, auxiliary-loss-free balancing, and multi-token prediction. The reported MacBook Air run trained a 36.2-million-parameter model on detective fiction in about 2.6 hours. It is an educational architecture demo rather than a production language model.

webdev.title: Introducing UI SDK
webdev.summary: UI SDK provides more than 50 TypeScript behaviors for keyboard navigation, focus, selection, popups, drag and drop, and the associated ARIA attributes. Developers and agents can compose them into custom components or use ready-made libraries for React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, and Web Components. Agent interaction can be limited through developer-defined permissions, and the library remains in beta.

webdev.title: The Console Framework
webdev.summary: Text.js lets developers build React applications that render inside the browser's DevTools console. One app can run in the browser console, in a terminal, or through MCP for coding agents.

webdev.title: A Family Tree of Software Job Titles
webdev.summary: An interactive family tree traces 104 software job titles from human computers to AI agent and context engineers across seven role families. It highlights how responsibilities split, recombine, and reappear under new names, including the overlap among DevOps, SRE, and platform engineering. Dates indicate roughly when titles became common and are estimates rather than a sourced chronology.

webdev.title: Declarative Dragging
webdev.summary: Declarative dragging lets developers specify which future application states an element should reach, then renders those states to synthesize drop zones and animated interactions. Dragology implements the approach for SVG interfaces on the web, with composable behaviors and modifiers for snapping and transitions. The project received a UIST 2026 Best Paper award.

webdev.title: The only web search APIs built for high growth AI
webdev.summary: Parallel gives your agents the freshest, most accurate web results in less than 200ms, from $1 per 1,000 searches. Harvey, Notion and Rogo run it in production. Start building for free .

webdev.title: PyPI's redesigned project pages with clearer security signals
webdev.summary: PyPI's redesigned pages add a security tab for release-file attestations and warnings about missing, inconsistent, changed, or lost provenance, while making clear that absent provenance alone does not mean a package is malicious.

webdev.title: Eclipse Mosquitto
webdev.summary: Mosquitto implements MQTT 5.0, 3.1.1, and 3.1, with C and C++ client libraries plus command-line tools for publishing, subscribing, and broker administration.

webdev.title: Protomaps: Self-hosting map tiles has gotten cheap and easy
webdev.summary: This post walks through how to deploy a single PMTiles archive to object storage and serve map tiles through HTTP Range requests.

devops.title: 📈 Users spike. Your stress level doesn't have to.
devops.summary: Traffic surges are supposed to be good news. But when your infrastructure can't keep up, that "we're going viral 🎉" moment can easily turn into “everything is down and needs fixing right now.” 👉 Ditch the stress-coding with Microsoft Azure. Azure autoscales and optimizes performance behind the scenes, so you can roll out features without worrying about downtime or slowdowns. 🌎 With more global regions than any other cloud provider, Azure gives you the headroom to grow — without the growing pains. Take the stress out of scaling with Azure 😌

devops.title: Introducing Spend Management: Spending limits and alerts for Cloudflare
devops.summary: Cloudflare's new Spend Management feature lets pay-as-you-go customers set spending thresholds and pause activity when limits are reached to avoid unexpected bills. The beta supports Workers and Durable Objects and provides near real-time cost monitoring in the dashboard, CLI, and API.

devops.title: Announcing kagent 1.0 GA
devops.summary: kagent 1.0 is an enterprise-ready distribution of Agent Substrate for running AI agents on Kubernetes. The system addresses pod-per-agent limitations by scheduling agent workloads as "actors" on warm worker pools, automatically suspending idle actors to free up compute and restoring them when new requests arrive. Agent Substrate is now a CNCF project.

devops.title: Throwing Out The Phonebook
devops.summary: Fly.io redesigned its 6PN private network, replacing a synchronized "phonebook" of hundreds of thousands of routing entries on every host with a lazy lookup system. The new design stores only 100 to 200 records per host, learning routes on demand when machines initiate connections. This approach uses VXLAN and standard kernel components instead of complex eBPF logic, which simplifies debugging and improves reliability.

devops.title: Gang scheduling and topology-aware placement for AI training in Kubernetes
devops.summary: Distributed AI training workloads require pods to land on hardware with the right inter-GPU bandwidth and to be scheduled simultaneously. Kubernetes' built-in scheduler cannot meet these requirements as it schedules pods individually. Topology-aware scheduling and gang scheduling, implemented by Kueue and the Coscheduling plugin, solve these placement and coordination problems.

devops.title: Put every SaaS tenant behind its own VM boundary
devops.summary: ISVs often give each customer a dedicated environment just to keep tenants apart, which wastes capacity. AWS Nitro Sandboxes lets Amazon EKS and Amazon ECS bin-pack multiple tenants onto shared nodes, each in a hardware-isolated sandbox with its own kernel. For sensitive tenants, confidential mode adds attestation that proves data stays private from operators and AWS. See how it works here .

devops.title: Airgorah
devops.summary: Airgorah is a WiFi security auditing tool that captures traffic, performs deauthentication attacks, and cracks access point passwords. It is written in Rust with a GTK4 interface and runs on Linux. The tool requires a wireless network card that supports monitor mode and packet injection.

devops.title: Uptime Kuma
devops.summary: Uptime Kuma is a self-hosted monitoring tool that tracks uptime for HTTP(s), TCP, DNS records, and Docker containers. It features a reactive UI, supports over 90 notification services including Telegram and Slack, and lets users create multiple status pages.

devops.title: Google Open-Sources TPU Sync for KV Cache and Weight Transfer on TPUs
devops.summary: Google Cloud open sourced TPU Sync, a C++ library that moves KV cache blocks and model weights between TPU memory, host memory, and storage. It cut median KV transfer latency for Qwen3 235B from several seconds to about 230 ms.

devops.title: HTTPd (CVE-2026-119618): Detecting heap corruption and RCE in Apache HTTP Server mod_http2
devops.summary: Apache fixed CVE-2026-119618, a critical heap corruption flaw in mod_http2 that can lead to remote code execution, with the release of HTTP Server 2.4.71 on November 11. The vulnerability affects versions 2.4.55 through 2.4.70, requires no authentication to exploit, and received a 9.8 severity score from Red Hat. A public proof-of-concept demonstrates heap corruption, but no remote code execution exploit has been released.

devops.title: 6 questions to ask before connecting an MCP server
devops.summary: SaaS vendors get a security review. MCP servers often go to production with privileged credentials in minutes. Read the 6 questions to ask before you connect.

devops.title: Powering agentic cloud governance: What's new in Organization Policy
devops.summary: Google Cloud made its Organization Policy MCP server generally available and added Gemini-powered natural language authoring of custom constraints.

devops.title: Meta Wins CNCF End User Case Study Contest for Accelerating AI Infrastructure Deployments From Hours to Minutes
devops.summary: Meta's Cloud Foundation team won the CNCF End User Case Study Contest for a GitOps platform built on Argo CD and Kargo across about 100 clusters.

devops.title: Degrade gracefully: designing AI features that keep working when the model doesn't
devops.summary: Skyscanner and incident.io both chose graceful degradation as their top AI resilience investment.

data.title: Clean up your files first. Get 46% more accurate answers
data.summary: In our benchmark, that came from just one change: removing duplicate files. Deasy scans and enriches your files before they go to AI, catching old versions, contradictions, and sensitive details before they become answers. All in minutes. Then, put the clean files to work. Publish curated files to Databricks or push metadata back into SharePoint so Copilot can find the right file faster. Or quickly set up a queryable vector DB. See it →

data.title: The Future of Data Science and Analytics Engineering at Klaviyo
data.summary: AI can produce code and analysis faster than people can review it at Klaviyo, making human attention and clear ownership the main bottlenecks. Data science and analytics engineering are merging into a broader role focused on guiding AI, checking its work, and turning useful findings into action.

data.title: Read Less, Solve More: Token-Efficient Sparse Reading for AI Agents
data.summary: SparseRead is a training-free control layer that decides how much of a file, webpage, or repository enters an agent's context. Its read gate, bounded evidence packs, and explicit raw fallback target the common read-everything pattern. The authors report lower token use and latency without changing the model across six models and five workloads.

data.title: How Pinterest Improved Analytics Agent Compliance with Loop Engineering
data.summary: Pinterest's Analytics Agent can skip required steps, such as inspecting table metadata before writing SQL. Manual instruction edits left one rule at 64% compliance, so the team built loop engineering: propose a change, test it on paired test suites, and keep what works. The first large run reached 89.3% compliance, though 10.3% of cases changed verdict between runs.

data.title: Data governance that actually runs
data.summary: Governance-as-code turns policy into checks across a local, open-source stack: MinIO for S3-like intake; Postgres for operations and warehousing; Airflow 3 and dbt for pipelines; DataHub, Apache Ossie, and Superset for catalog, semantic definitions, and dashboards; and MCP-connected AI assistants. CI enforces contracts, ownership, masking, lineage, consumer-impact approval, and least-privilege access before production.

data.title: Do Data Roles Have a Future?
data.summary: This post splits data work into production, interpretation, and accountability, and argues AI makes production dramatically cheaper while the other two stay human. In the 2026 Practical Data Community Survey, 80% of respondents used AI daily. Only about 10% had built it into organisational workflows, and nearly 89% still wrestled with basic data modelling.

data.title: How Open Is Open? Iceberg, Catalogs, and User Choice
data.summary: Open table formats do not by themselves make a lakehouse portable: an Iceberg catalog's support for commits, metadata loading, planning, concurrent writers, and credentials can still create hard-to-see dependencies. The proposal is a deployable community baseline built around the REST catalog protocol, Apache Polaris, compatibility testing, performance benchmarks, and tested migration procedures, so teams can verify what they can run, swap, and take with them.

data.title: Your Business Users Already Have an AI Analyst. Do Their Numbers Match Yours?
data.summary: Ask an AI assistant for active customers using three different exports and you get three confident answers. In a Databox survey of 100+ business users, 86% reach for an AI assistant first, yet only 39% fully trust it for analysis shared with leadership. Timextender's new field guide gives data teams four principles for owning what the numbers mean, and a known-answer test to run this week. At B&S , the BI team cleared an enormous data backlog within 6 to 12 months of moving to Timextender, and new requests now take one to two days. See how in a demo →

data.title: Auto Ontology: Grounding Agents in Enterprise Data
data.summary: NVIDIA's Apache-licensed Auto Ontology turns database metadata into a semantic graph that humans can review and certify, and agents can access over MCP, API, or CLI. It maps business terms, certified SQL attributes, and relationships to underlying data so it can generate queries and disclose their provenance. The aim is to make natural-language analytics more consistent and auditable than direct text-to-SQL.

data.title: db-branch
data.summary: db-branch is a self-hosted, open-source tool that creates isolated MySQL and PostgreSQL database copies in seconds, sharing existing storage until changes are made. It lets developers and AI agents test queries, migrations, and upgrades without changing production data, with options to reset, restore, or automatically delete each copy.

data.title: PyPI's redesigned project pages with clearer security signals are now live
data.summary: PyPI has redesigned its package pages with a security tab showing where release files came from and warnings when that information is missing, inconsistent, or unexpectedly changed. Updated file lists and release histories make packages easier to assess, though verified origins do not guarantee safe code.

data.title: PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, 14.25, and 19 RC 2 Released!
data.summary: PostgreSQL shipped patch releases for all supported branches, fixing 52 security vulnerabilities and more than 140 bugs. PostgreSQL 14 is now end-of-life, so production teams should upgrade to a supported version. The updates are cumulative and usually straightforward, though some deployments may also need index rebuilds or a fresh full backup.

data.title: What thousands of conversations look like inside a language model
data.summary: An experiment mapped Qwen's internal representations of thousands of question-and-answer examples, finding overlapping regions shaped partly by language, with Chinese more visibly separated from English, German, Croatian, and Python code. The 3D maps captured only 17.6% of the full variation, showing how visualizations can reveal patterns while hiding much of the underlying complexity.

data.title: Real-time Alert in Spark
data.summary: UiPath built a Spark Structured Streaming alerting system that evaluates 20,000 alert definitions per minute, including windowed conditions and SLA checks, without repeatedly rescanning source data. The key design was joining streams to static definitions once and managing state carefully, which cut memory from 12 GB to 4 GB and reduced downstream network calls.

data.title: Join Chalk's webinar and learn how to run coding agents in scalable sandboxes, in your cloud
data.summary: Explore how Chalk Sandboxes, Functions, and Volumes enable isolated agent sessions, secure access to tools and resources, persistent shared context, and parallel development at scale. Register here

data.title: Outbox Pattern in Postgres: Concurrent Workers vs Reading the WAL
data.summary: For Postgres outbox delivery, polling is simplest, but WAL-based logical replication delivered the best throughput and lowest latency, while trigger-time NOTIFY caused severe contention under load.

data.title: Postgres not using your index? It's counting pages, not rows
data.summary: Postgres often ignores an index because it estimates page reads, not row counts, and low-selectivity filters can still touch most heap pages.

design.title: Five New Google Flow Tools Designed by Visual Artists
design.summary: Five new tools land in Google Flow, the AI creative studio, each built by a working artist or filmmaker. Character Poster and Character Arc keep characters consistent in style and across ages, while Pixel Machine adds bitmap, ASCII, CRT, and glitch looks. Lucid Glass simulates prisms and refractions no real lens can capture, and Pocket Studio turns a single phone take into multiple polished camera angles.

design.title: Google announces Gemini 4 Hydrogen with ‘significant leaps' in speed, intelligence
design.summary: Google has introduced Gemini 4 Hydrogen, replacing the Flash branding with a model designed to deliver higher intelligence and faster performance at an accessible price. Compared with Gemini 3.8 Flash, Hydrogen reportedly completes tasks 2.5 times faster at its default high setting, more than triples its Terminal-Bench 4.1 score, and reduces fabricated claims by over fivefold. It also supports a native one-million-token input and output context, with improvements in tool recovery, multimodal reasoning, and complex agentic workflows.

design.title: Adobe's AI Experiments Let You Walk Around in Photos and Interview Your Characters
design.summary: Adobe's experimental “sneaks” at its Max conference include AI tools that turn photos into explorable 3D scenes, let users interview characters, and make edits copy-pasteable. Screen Test shapes AI characters' personalities through conversation, while Sight Span turns flat images into navigable 3D spaces. Sound Bender generates cursor-adjustable audio and Rinse Repeat copies Photoshop edits to other subjects, though these tech previews may never become Creative Cloud or Firefly features.

design.title: Design is a Search Problem
design.summary: Design is a search problem: finding the right solution in a vast space of possibilities, which computer science's search algorithms help explain. Beam search mirrors the "show me some options" approach that AI has made far wider, while A* matches a more deliberate process steered by a good heuristic. AI has widened the beam without improving the heuristic, so empathy and taste remain the human edge.

design.title: Build Faster Without Leaving Accessibility Behind
design.summary: The newly open-sourced Accessibility Considerations Toolkit (ACT) helps teams find barriers before AI-assisted development repeats the same mistakes across more interfaces, faster. It pairs access strategies and assistive technologies with usability heuristics and standards references, in Markdown for people and YAML for agents and pipelines. ACT doesn't replace testing with disabled people or establish compliance, and its findings still need human review.

design.title: Every click has a price now. Who designs how that “feels”?
design.summary: As AI products shift toward credit- and usage-based pricing, everyday interactions increasingly carry a visible financial cost, creating new challenges for user experience design. Unpredictable charges, unclear token consumption, and sudden usage limits can undermine trust, making transparent cost estimates, spending controls, and understandable feedback essential interface features. Designers must also decide when expensive AI processing is justified and when simpler alternatives can deliver the same result without introducing unnecessary cost or anxiety.

design.title: Reach 8 million tech professionals reading TLDR
design.summary: Ads get ignored on social media but not in TLDR! Reach designers and design leaders where they actually pay attention. Learn more about sponsorship opportunities .

design.title: Protect Human Writing by Poisoning Unauthorized AI Training
design.summary: Publish for humans, not for crawlers. A web font that swaps the words in your HTML, so readers see your writing and scrapers get a decoy copy.

design.title: Neumorphism CSS Generator
design.summary: Easily generate soft UI and Neumorphism CSS styles. Customize colors and shadows, then copy the code.

design.title: Everything You've Saved, in One Visual Library
design.summary: One visual library for everything you save on Instagram, X, TikTok, Pinterest, and more. Tagged by AI, searchable by meaning and color, and kept even when the post is gone.

design.title: Circuit: Civic Shuttle Brand Identity by The Collected Works
design.summary: The Collected Works has redesigned Circuit, an electric shuttle service operating across 50 cities, to replace its fragmented local identities with a cohesive brand inspired by dependable public infrastructure. The refreshed system retains Circuit's original C symbol, introduces Stadt and Haffer typography, and uses directional arrows, road-inspired graphics, and a restrained green palette to evoke urban transportation. A custom generative tool creates continuous route-like graphics, while standardized fleet wraps and flexible local messaging help the identity remain consistent across different cities.

design.title: Bruno's HelloAsso identity follows France's love of brands with values
design.summary: Bruno has rebranded HelloAsso, a free platform serving 480,000 French nonprofits, with a new identity built around the idea of individuals coming together to form a collective. Its central graphic device is a mosaic of real member portraits, where individual squares can split to accommodate text, supported by bold Franklin Gothic typography, candid photography, and an expressive color palette. The system extends across HelloAsso Sport, Generosity, Culture, and its Fund for Engagement, giving each offering a distinctive visual personality while maintaining a recognizable shared identity.

design.title: Japanese Logos: 43 Classic Logo Designs and the Stories Behind Them
design.summary: Japanese graphic design produced some of the world's most influential corporate identities between the 1960s and early 1990s, with designers including Yusaku Kamekura, Ikko Tanaka, Kazumasa Nagai, and Takenobu Igarashi. Forty-three classic logos spanning Sony, NTT, Japan Airlines, Mazda, and the Tokyo 1964 Olympics demonstrate how modernist geometry, cultural symbolism, and distinctive visual ideas helped establish recognizable identities. Many also emerged from strategic corporate identity programs, particularly those developed by PAOS, that connected visual design with broader organizational transformation.

design.title: Band-Aid Accessibility
design.summary: More disabled people are using LLM coding tools to build the accessible features and apps mainstream software never delivered.

design.title: Brand Insistence: Why the Strongest Brands Have No Substitutes
design.summary: The strongest brands push customers past preference and loyalty to insistence, where they'll wait, search, or pay more because there's no substitute.

design.title: The toy company Tomy has a new logo, and people are baffled
design.summary: Japanese toymaker Tomy is adopting the unified global name Takara Tomy and replacing its familiar blue-and-white logo with a new identity featuring a teal-to-magenta gradient symbol inspired by the Japanese characters for "asobi" (play).

marketing.title: 75% of marketers can't say what share of their promotions is profitable
marketing.summary: This is one of the numbers behind Pecan's 2027 B2C Growth Predictions - built on 2026 research from Gartner, Recurly, Kantar, and others. Pecan predicts: Churn reports become weekly early warnings. 4.25% monthly churn compounds to 41% YoY. Predicted LTV replaces ROAS. Advertisers bidding on value already see 12% higher ROAS on Meta. Discounts get rationed by uplift, not handed to customers who would have bought anyway. 🔮 Read all 10 predictions (free and ungated) and the moves you need to make this quarter to prepare. 👉 Get a demo of Pecan to see which of your customers will churn, buy or grow

marketing.title: The only way to go is down
marketing.summary: Americans spend more than 13 hours a day consuming media, but only 25 hours a week receive their full attention. As media consumption grows, focused attention is shrinking. Social media and in-person entertainment are gaining a larger share of that attention. These channels have something in common. They encourage shared interests and community connection rather than passive consumption. The trend points to a growing divide between content that fills people's time and experiences that earn their attention.

marketing.title: The Death of Owned Marketing
marketing.summary: AI agents are changing how buyers discover and evaluate brands. Brand perception increasingly forms through third-party sources like customer reviews and online communities rather than company websites. Positioning needs to stay consistent across these sources, while original research should offer unique insights that earn independent citations. Brands should also test how AI tools recommend their products. As agents take on more of the buying process, pricing and checkout need to be accessible without human navigation.

marketing.title: 6 tips on creator marketing
marketing.summary: Gamma's creator marketing drove 32% of signups as the company scaled to $100M ARR. Its growth lead recommends measuring results across creator cohorts since individual post performance is highly unpredictable. Allocate 70% of budget to lower-cost creators and use platform-specific agencies. Track attribution through onboarding surveys rather than links. Refresh creative to prevent audience fatigue and combine professional creators and existing customers to balance reach.

marketing.title: Show Online What Shoppers Can't Touch
marketing.summary: Product images can recreate the in-store experience by showing shoppers textures and details they cannot experience online. Backdrop and Fireclay Tile use close-up photography and directional lighting to highlight surface details that flat color swatches miss. Lush Cosmetics shows bath bombs dissolving in water and scrubs spread out to demonstrate their consistency. Feature texture and product details early in the gallery, then use in-action images to show how products look and behave when used.

marketing.title: How to take your best hook to another country
marketing.summary: Subtitled hooks rarely travel, since they run on local jokes and references that translation strips out. Expansion works best one country at a time, starting where the app already ranks without any content. Some hooks only need a local store or city swapped in, while an in-joke that lands in one language needs a full rewrite. Local creators then film in their own dialect, with the app kept out of the first 2 seconds of the video.

marketing.title: Your legacy CMS isn't just painful to use. It's costing you
marketing.summary: Marketing teams are being asked to deliver more, faster, and make every dollar work harder. At the same time, most website infrastructure makes even routine work unnecessarily difficult. When a simple update takes multiple teams and weeks of handoffs, something's gone wrong . Read the website modernization guide on the Wix Enterprise blog (free and ungated).

marketing.title: Turn 1-Hour Into 64 Pieces of Content, with Hiten Shah (Webinar)

marketing.title: How to Build an AI Customer Research Agent in Claude Code (59 minute video)
marketing.summary: This podcast episode explains how to build an AI customer research agent in Claude Code to uncover why people abandon sign-up or cancel. The agent emails customers at key drop-off points using customer data from a CSV and custom instructions. It asks one question at a time, then categorizes replies and connects feedback to purchase behavior. In one example, Ancestry found that shipping concerns were a bigger conversion barrier than subscription fees. An LLM judge checks that replies are grounded in company documentation before sending.

marketing.title: The Dutch Broadcaster That Stopped Tracking Its Viewers and Made More Money
marketing.summary: Personalization doesn't always improve ad performance, and third-party tracking may add less value than the industry claims. Dutch broadcaster NPO eliminated third-party cookies and sold ads based on content and context instead, increasing ad revenue by 61%. Research found tracking added only 4% to publisher revenue. A travel site experiment found generic brand ads outperformed retargeting ads featuring hotels shoppers had viewed. Personalized ads performed better after shoppers visited a review site and narrowed their choices.

marketing.title: How I Built an AI Marketing Team With Grok Bot Without Writing Code
marketing.summary: A solo founder uses specialized AI bots to run marketing tasks on a schedule. Each bot has one defined role and follows a shared rules file with factual checks and clear limits. The marketing bot drafts content but requires human approval before anything is published. A weekly report adds lessons and updates instructions so future jobs improve. Batching content into a 21-day calendar reduces daily planning, while a separate bot checks actual outputs and flags stalled work.

marketing.summary: ChatGPT Wallet lets select US Pro subscribers aged 18+ use AI agents to shop and complete purchases.

Sellers of bigger contracts should check where their buyers' budgets went, because OpenAI and Anthropic have more than tripled their revenue this year.

Shopify takes the same cut no matter who clicks buy, so it opened checkout to agents in September. Stores that live on upsells can respond by raising base prices or charging agents a fee at checkout.

founders.title: Don't Neglect the M&A Path

It's important to start early to improve your chances that M&A remains an option. This post is the first of a three-part series that covers preparing for M&A, the M&A process, and diligence and closing.

founders.title: Less time on code, more time on architecture
founders.summary: Clay relies on AI review agents to catch routine bugs in most pull requests, freeing engineers to focus on decisions that are risky or hard to reverse, such as changing a data schema or deciding which service owns a piece of logic. For complex changes, engineers discuss the design before reviewing the code in detail. If a large pull request arrives without that context, reviewers ask for a short design write-up and pause the review until the team has discussed it.

founders.title: Ask Claude which of your shipped work moved a number
founders.summary: Building with AI feels productive because something ships every day. founders.title: Most of AI moats are just fuel

Moats are defined by their ability to provide lasting protection without ongoing resource inputs, unlike fuel, which only provides a competitive edge when continuously added. Reinforcing loops, such as network and data effects, can evolve into moats by reducing dependency on fuel, making businesses harder to challenge.

crypto.title: House Oversight Chair looks to ban govt officials' prediction market bets
crypto.summary: Chair James Comer released findings from a May investigation covering 1,700 pages of documents and five briefings from prediction market firms, and urges legislation restricting what bets federal employees, lawmakers, and staff can place, up to an outright ban. The probe follows an Army soldier's Polymarket bets on Maduro's capture and a White House teleprompter operator profiting on Kalshi. Kalshi and Polymarket say they have tightened controls, and the Senate passed a resolution in April banning members from such trading.

crypto.title: Kava Lend loses about $3.8 million to hack, KAVA token down nearly 40%
crypto.summary: An attacker drained about 55.2M KAVA (~$3.76M at pre-attack prices) by exploiting a dormant BUSD market, shrinking its net supply to a tiny nonzero figure so deposit values inflated ~243,000-fold, then borrowing KAVA against it 127 times. About 49.2M KAVA was bridged to BNB Chain through LayerZero and sold for about $2.1M. The attacker had been preparing since November 8. Kava says it is “not an infinite mint” and is contained to Kava Lend, has paused the Axelar bridge, and promises a full incident report. KAVA was down about 39% at publication, and exchanges paused deposits and withdrawals.

crypto.title: Tempo Configurable Accounts: PQ + Native Multisig as Default
crypto.summary: Tempo's Configurable Accounts (T14) will deploy to mainnet on December 1, introducing post-quantum signature groundwork and native multisig as default account primitives rather than optional add-ons. The upgrade's core claim is friction elimination: both capabilities existed on prior systems, but Configurable Accounts makes them cheap enough to use without weighing cost against benefit. Paradigm frames T14 as a near-completion milestone in "Pragmatic Native Account Abstraction" for the Ethereum ecosystem, with one remaining component, Attestable Accounts, expected in the coming weeks.

crypto.title: ChatGPT Wallet Launches for Agentic Commerce
crypto.summary: OpenAI's ChatGPT Wallet, launched Friday, lets OpenAI's always-on agent check out on merchant sites using your own credit card. At checkout, the card network generates a one-time substitute card number capped at the approved amount, so the agent never holds your real card, and you keep your points and dispute rights. Issuers gain visibility versus wallets like Stripe's Link, which charge your card in a second transaction, and merchants may pay lower interchange and see who is buying. Users review and approve each purchase with Face ID, and it is limited to US ChatGPT Pro users 18 or older with Amex, Mastercard, or Visa credit cards only. Under the hood, it uses a vault, enrollment in the networks' agent programs (Visa Intelligent Commerce, Mastercard Agent Pay, and Amex ACE), and two sets of headers: Web Bot Auth signatures and user signals in the Forwarded header, with OpenAI working with fraud providers like Forter, Riskified, Sardine, and Signifyd to honor them. Drawbacks are sites still blocking agents, the per-purchase approval, partial card coverage, and slow, token-heavy browser checkout.

crypto.title: The Antifragile Internet
crypto.summary: October 2026's incident cluster (PHP2Shell exposing 5M+ hosts, Railway decrypting secrets across 100K workspaces, Binance losing $6.3B, and eMudhra issuing a signing key set to "4") frames the argument that AI has collapsed the cost of exploitation to near zero. There are three agent-specific threat vectors: agents as weapons, agents as targets, and agents as impostors. USV's investment thesis closes on crypto: blockchains proved strangers can transact without mutual trust, and the firm expects decentralized reputation, PAP/A2A agent-identity protocols, and permissionless rails to embed in mainstream apps as a two-lane internet takes shape.

crypto.title: How We Made $6M+ Exploiting a Single Onchain Edge
crypto.summary: A trader and collaborators extracted $6M+ from two Robinhood Chain listings by monitoring two public data sources: Wintermute's on-chain market-making contract whitelists and BitGo's GitHub repository (Robinhood's custody partner). For cashcat, a "hoodeth:cashcat" string in a public BitGo pull request on July 27 and Wintermute's WETH pool approval on August 3 at 17:48 UTC gave days of advance notice. The group accumulated over $1M at around 4% of supply and realized $4M+ when Robinhood listed three days later. A parallel pipeline applied to PONS produced another $2M, with the method requiring no privileged access, only structured monitoring of public contract approval events and custody provider repositories.

crypto.title: Nexo report shows government payments dominate its card by value
crypto.summary: Alex highlights Nexo's card report: 91% of government payments exceed €1,000, 55% fall between €5,000 and €10,000, and nearly 12% exceed the €10,000 daily limit. He estimates the average government payment at about €6,400 against €80 for the average card transaction, and notes millennials make up about 42% of them. it.title: AI recovery needs more than an undo button
it.summary: Restoring an AI agent, reversing its changes to internal systems, and undoing its business consequences are three different problems. Commvault's recovery tools address parts of the first two, but actions such as sending customer emails or supplier orders still require controls before execution.

it.title: AWS Secrets Manager now supports cross-account replication
it.summary: AWS Secrets Manager now supports cross-account replication, allowing teams to maintain synchronized copies of primary secrets across AWS accounts for backup, disaster recovery, and cross-account access. The feature extends multi-Region replication across account boundaries, enabling centralized ownership and rotation without shared KMS keys or cross-account policies.

it.title: Claude joins meetings with Granola and Otter integrations planned

Upcoming integrations with Granola, Gong, Attention, Fireflies.ai, Otter, and Plaud will let teams send meeting transcripts to their existing tools.

it.title: Nvidia, AMD, Google, and Meta join open inference consortium

Members will contribute deployment feedback, testing resources, and development work, while SGLang's maintainers retain control over technical decisions.

it.title: Marvell targets AI's memory and networking bottlenecks
it.summary: Marvell is showcasing optical interconnects, CXL memory expansion, and networking technology at Supercomputing 2026. The demonstrations focus on scaling memory and compute across racks to address bandwidth constraints and infrastructure underutilization.

it.title: Building always-on agents
it.summary: The architecture for always-on agents relies on five primary primitives: an event inbox, durable timers, persistent memory, a permission system, and an outbound communication outbox. The framework is designed to enable AI agents to operate autonomously in the background while maintaining stateful and proactive behaviour.
